ai.description: This frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brown with a distinct mid-dorsal stripe and dark transverse bars on the limbs. It is identified by its long, slender hind limbs and a pointed, narrow snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya syhadrensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent glandular fold (dorsolateral ridge) running along its back.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya syhadrensis* inhabits moist grasslands, paddy fields, and scrub forests across the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Minervarya syhadrensis* is primarily nocturnal, often emerging after monsoon rains to forage for small insects near water bodies and damp, grassy habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya syhadrensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 150–400 eggs in shallow water. The eggs hatch into aquatic larvae that undergo metamorphosis.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya syhadrensis* is found across the Western Ghats and parts of the Deccan Plateau in India, typically inhabiting elevations from near sea level up to 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Minervarya syhadrensis* is a series of rapid, high-pitched, insect-like chirps typically heard near shallow, temporary rain pools and marshes.
